1	# NINEONELABS RENEWALD
2	
3	NineOneLabs 웹에이전시 사이트 리뉴얼 프로젝트입니다.
4	
5	## 📚 문서
6	
7	- 아키텍처·규칙: `.claude/rules/` (php.md, frontend.md, scss.md)
8	- 스킬: `.claude/skills/` (migration, new-route)
9	- 에이전트: `.claude/agents/` (php-explorer, scene-explorer)

11	## 🚀 빠른 시작

271	## 🚢 배포
272	
273	### 서버 배포 시 주의사항
274	
275	**중요**: 서버 배포 시 `vendor/` 폴더가 프로젝트에 포함되어야 합니다.
276	
277	```bash
278	# 1. 프로덕션 빌드
279	npm run build
280	
281	# 2. Composer 패키지 설치 (vendor/ 폴더 생성)
282	make composer
283	# 또는
284	composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader
285	
286	# 3. 프로젝트 전체를 서버에 업로드
287	# - vendor/ 폴더 포함

291	### 배포 시 포함해야 할 파일/폴더
292	
293	- ✅ `vendor/` - Composer 패키지 (필수)

1	# NINEONELABS Codex Guide
2	
3	Use this file for Codex-specific repo instructions. Keep Claude-specific behavior in `CLAUDE.md`.
4	
5	## Brand Identity
6	
7	See `/BRAND.md` for the complete brand identity reference. Read it before writing any copy, section names, headlines, CTAs, or storytelling.
8	
9	Key rules:
10	
11	- Company: **NineOneLabs (나인원랩스)** — digital web agency
12	- Core values: **Experiment · Challenge · Proof** (실험 · 도전 · 증명)
13	- Concept: Earth → Planet NX-2 voyage. NineOneLabs is the companion (조력자), not the captain.
14	- Slogan: **JOIN THE JOURNEY** — use as-is for display contexts
15	- Services: APP · WEB · BRANDING · UI/UX · MAINTENANCE
16	- Space metaphor is the frame, not the message — always land on the concrete agency offer
17	- Never position NineOneLabs as an aerospace/aviation entity
18	
19	## Project Defaults
20	
21	- Stack: TypeScript, SCSS, Three.js, Vite, PHP 7.4 custom MVC, MySQL, Apache via Docker
22	- Dev server: `http://localhost:8888`
23	- Default task framing: state the goal, relevant context, constraints, and done condition.
24	- For complex or ambiguous work, plan first before editing code.
25	- Prefer `chop` for long git, typecheck, and Docker inspection output when available.
26	- For read-only `git` inspection commands that may produce non-trivial output, prefer `chop` by default.
27	- Typical examples: `chop git status`, `chop git diff`, `chop git log --oneline -20`.
28	- Prefer `chop rg ...` for repository searches when the result may be longer than a few lines.
29	- For PowerShell builtins or pipeline-based inspection commands, wrap the whole script with `chop powershell -Command "..."`.
30	- Typical examples: `chop powershell -Command "Get-Content ... | Select-Object -Skip 720 -First 90"` and `chop powershell -Command "Get-Content ... | Select-String ..."`.
31	- Very short one-line commands may skip `chop`, but when in doubt prefer `chop`.
32	- **Do not run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install`** — Vite dev server auto-rebuilds the bundle on every file save; there is no reason to run these. Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when explicitly adding a new dependency.
33	- Do not add any of these commands to agent roles, task plans, verification steps, or PR notes unless the user explicitly asks for it.
34	- On Windows PowerShell, use explicit UTF-8 for Korean text reads and writes.
35	
36	## Architecture
37	
38	- Public routes stay closure-based in `routes/web.php` and render via `render()`.
39	- Do not reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation contracts.
40	- Do not duplicate ownership already handled by `AppManager`, `PageRuntime`, or `PageTheatreBinder`.
41	- Keep shared engine or runtime code out of page folders.
42	- Put page scene code in `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`.
43	- Put Theatre bindings in `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`.
44	- Keep shared types in `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`.
45	
46	## Editing Rules
47	
48	- Follow existing custom MVC patterns; do not introduce Laravel or Symfony conventions.
49	- Use BEM-style naming in SCSS.
50	- Keep admin CSS and JS separate from the public SCSS pipeline.
51	- For SCSS responsive sizing, prefer shared abstract helpers such as `fluid(...)` instead of ad-hoc raw values when the project already uses that pattern.
52	- Use `#{fluid(...)}` only inside shared `abstract` or `base` files when emitting CSS custom properties or shared tokens.
53	- In component, layout, and page SCSS files, use `fluid(min, max)` directly instead of `#{fluid(...)}`.
54	- In SCSS files outside `resource/scss/abstract/` and `resource/scss/base/`, add `@use "../abstract" as *;` at the top before using shared helpers like `fluid(...)`.
55	- Do not use CSS variable fallbacks like `var(--token, fallback)` in SCSS. Use either `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly.
56	- Do not introduce base/root tokens unless the value is genuinely shared across multiple features. Avoid token waste for one-off component values.
57	- For reusable SCSS values, define the source of truth in the shared `abstract` or `base` layer first, then reference it from component or page partials.
58	- Prefer semantic tokens over raw hex values when an upstream token exists.
59	- Dispose Three.js geometries, materials, and textures.
60	- Avoid object creation inside render loops.
61	- Match event listener registration with cleanup.
62	- Never hardcode credentials or secrets.
63	
64	## Verification
65	
66	- TypeScript: `chop node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`

1	# NINEONELABS — Brand Identity
2	
3	> **For AI agents:** Always read this file before writing copy, naming sections, proposing storytelling directions, or suggesting UI text for this project. This is the single source of truth for brand identity.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Company
8	
9	| | |
10	|---|---|
11	| **Name (EN)** | NineOneLabs |
12	| **Name (KR)** | 나인원랩스 |
13	| **Type** | Digital Web Agency |
14	| **Location** | Korea |
15	| **Founded** | — |
16	
17	NineOneLabs is a digital web agency that designs immersive brand experiences. We build websites, apps, and brand identities — not as a deliverable, but as the beginning of a journey clients take with us.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Core Values
22	
23	| Value | Korean | Meaning |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| **Experiment** | 실험 | We test unconventional ideas. Tried-and-safe is not our mode. |
26	| **Challenge** | 도전 | We take on briefs others won't. Difficulty is a reason to proceed. |
27	| **Proof** | 증명 | Results matter. Every claim we make, we demonstrate. |
28	
29	These three values — **실험 · 도전 · 증명** — are the foundation for all brand decisions, copy framing, and storytelling. When proposing headlines or messaging, anchor them to at least one of these values.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## Brand Concept & Narrative
34	
35	### The Journey Metaphor
36	
37	The central metaphor is **a voyage from Earth to Planet NX-2** — an unknown destination that represents the brand's potential, not yet discovered.
38	
39	- **Earth** = where the client starts (existing brand, current state)
40	- **NX-2** = the destination (realized potential, transformed brand, new audience)
41	- **NineOneLabs** = the crew, the Mission Control, the companion — not the captain. The client leads their story; we engineer the vessel.
42	
43	### The Role of NineOneLabs
44	
45	We are the **조력자 (facilitator/companion)** — not a vendor, not a service provider. We join the client's journey and share ownership of the outcome.
46	
47	This means:
48	- Copy should frame us alongside the client, not above or below
49	- Use "we" and "together" language, not "we will do X for you"
50	- The journey belongs to the client; we make it possible
51	
52	### Planet NX-2
53	
54	NX-2 is a coined name — it is intentionally mysterious, uncharted. It does not refer to a real place. It signals that where we're going together has never been mapped before.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Slogan
59	
60	```
61	JOIN THE JOURNEY
62	```
63	
64	- Always uppercase in display contexts
65	- Can be adapted as "Join The Journey" in title-case body copy
66	- Avoid abbreviating or paraphrasing — use as-is for CTAs and section anchors
67	- Variant in Korean: `함께 여정을 시작하세요` / `같은 여정을 함께 씁니다`
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Services
72	
73	| # | Name | Korean Description |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| 01 | **Web Build** | 사람들이 느끼고 오래 기억하는 웹. 브랜드만의 독창적인 인터랙션으로 특별한 경험을 설계합니다. |
76	| 02 | **App Build** | 브랜드는 화면 밖에서도 계속됩니다. 사용자가 편하게 쓰는 흐름을 중심으로, 손 안에서 완성되는 앱을 만듭니다. |
77	| 03 | **Branding** | 브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있어야 합니다. 핵심을 명확히 정리하고, 어디서나 같은 인상이 남는 정체성을 만듭니다. |
78	| 04 | **UI · UX** | 목적에 맞는 구조와 동선으로, 사용자가 편하고 자연스럽게 다음 행동으로 이어지게 설계합니다. |
79	| 05 | **Maintenance** | 서비스는 안정적으로 운영될 때 빛납니다. 구조를 정리하고, 문제가 생기기 전에 먼저 대응합니다. |
80	
81	**Short label set (for UI chips, tags, and skill lists):**
82	`APP` · `WEB` · `BRANDING` · `UI/UX` · `MAINTENANCE`
83	
84	---
85	
86	## Technology Strengths
87	
88	These are the capabilities we lead with. When explaining "why choose us," these are the proof points.
89	
90	| Technology | Category |
91	|---|---|
92	| **Three.js** | Interactive / Immersive Web |
93	| **GSAP** | Motion & Animation |
94	| **Webflow** | No-code CMS Build |
95	| **UI / UX Design** | User Experience |
96	| **Branding System** | Brand Identity |
97	| **3D Modeling** | Spatial Design |
98	| **SEO Strategy** | Search Growth |
99	| **CMS System** | Content Control |
100	| **TypeScript** | Engineering Quality |
101	| **PHP (Custom MVC)** | Backend Architecture |
102	
103	**Key differentiator:** We don't just use these tools — we apply them inside a unified, immersive experience. Our Three.js + GSAP stack is embedded in the actual site the client sees, not a demo.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## Visual Identity
108	
109	### Aesthetic Direction
110	
111	- **Dark, spatial, atmospheric** — the canvas is space; content floats in it
112	- **High contrast** — white type on deep backgrounds
113	- **Precision engineering** — sharp corners, controlled motion, no decorative noise
114	- **Immersive scroll** — the Three.js scene reacts to the user; nothing is static
115	
116	### Recurring Visual Elements
117	
118	| Element | Role |
119	|---|---|
120	| **Rocket** | Forward motion, launch, ambition — used for CTAs and transitions |
121	| **Planets / NX-2** | Destination, mystery, scale — used for hero and interstitial moments |
122	| **Astronaut** | The client/user in the journey — human scale against the cosmos |
123	| **Countdown / Mission Control UI** | The launch sequence metaphor — used in the `introAction` section |
124	| **Orbit rings** | Transition and motion markers |
125	
126	### Typography Style
127	
128	- EN display: uppercase, wide tracking, bold or regular weight
129	- KR body: medium/regular, sentence case
130	- Mixing EN headers with KR body is intentional — it's part of the brand voice
131	
132	---
133	
134	## Tone of Voice
135	
136	### Principles
137	
138	| Tone | Description |
139	|---|---|
140	| **Bold** | We don't hedge. "We design" not "we try to design." |
141	| **Experimental** | Willing to try sentence structures, punctuation, or framing that surprises. |
142	| **Precise** | Every word earns its place. No filler copy. |
143	| **Warm at scale** | We are a small team that handles big brands — intimate in conversation, confident in scope. |
144	| **Mission-language** | Borrow from aerospace: launch, orbit, mission, trajectory, control, signal. But use sparingly — never more than the content warrants. |
145	
146	### English Copy Style
147	
148	- Display headlines: title-case or ALL CAPS, 3–7 words preferred
149	- Subheadlines: sentence case, conversational
150	- Body: short paragraphs (2–3 lines), no complex clauses
151	- CTAs: verb-first, journey-anchored — "Start Your Journey", "Join The Mission", "Let's Launch"
152	
153	### Korean Copy Style
154	
155	- 존댓말(formal polite) for all public-facing copy
156	- Avoid corporate stiffness — write as a creative partner, not a firm
157	- Short sentences. Line breaks are intentional pacing, not overflow.
158	- Key phrases to use: `함께`, `여정`, `브랜드`, `설계`, `경험`, `나인원랩스`
159	- Key phrases to avoid: `솔루션`, `최고의`, `최적의`, `고객님` (too transactional)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## Content Guidelines
164	
165	### Section Narrative Arc (Homepage)
166	
167	The homepage tells a story in sequence — content should reinforce this arc:
168	
169	1. **Intro** — The invitation. "Your journey starts now." First contact with the brand.
170	2. **introAction** — The launch sequence. "Mission Control is live." The transition metaphor (Earth lift-off).
171	3. **Hero** — "Join The Journey." The slogan lands. We're in space now.
172	4. **Story** — Define the philosophy. Why we exist, what makes us different.
173	5. **Who** — Our role in your journey. We are the architects, not the pilots.
174	6. **Why (Skills)** — The proof. This is what we're capable of. Tech stack as credibility.
175	7. **Services** — What we build for you. Concrete, not abstract.
176	8. **Portfolio** — Evidence. Work that became real.
177	9. **Clients (Partners)** — Who has already trusted the journey.
178	10. **Contact** — "Your Journey Starts Here." The door is open.
179	
180	### Copy Rules
181	
182	- **Lead with the journey metaphor**, but always land on the concrete service or outcome
183	- **Never let the space concept obscure the agency offer** — every section must make it clear we build digital products
184	- **Avoid generic agency speak**: "passionate team", "cutting-edge solutions", "innovative approach"
185	- **Use the NX-2 narrative sparingly** — it's the frame, not every sentence
186	- Section titles should be able to stand alone as brand statements
187	
188	---
189	
190	## What We Are NOT
191	
192	These are active guardrails. If a content direction drifts toward any of these, correct course.
193	
194	| ❌ Avoid | ✅ Instead |
195	|---|---|
196	| Aerospace / aviation company | Web agency with a space-as-metaphor brand |
197	| Abstract art studio with no service clarity | Immersive web studio with defined deliverables |
198	| Generic "we're passionate creatives" agency | Results-driven team with Experiment · Challenge · Proof values |
199	| Overly poetic copy with no conversion intent | Bold copy that inspires AND directs to action |
200	| Trend-follower ("we use the latest AI tools!") | Craft-first ("we build what serves the brand") |
201	| "We do everything for you" positioning | "We journey together" partnership positioning |
202	
203	---
204	
205	## Glossary
206	
207	| Term | Usage |
208	|---|---|
209	| **NX-2** | The destination planet — a metaphor for the client's unrealized potential. Not a product name. |
210	| **Mission Control** | NineOneLabs in action — coordinating, engineering, keeping the mission on track. |
211	| **Launch** | Beginning of a project or brand reveal. |
212	| **Orbit** | The ongoing relationship after launch — maintenance, iteration, growth. |
213	| **Crew** | The NineOneLabs team. |
214	| **The Journey** | The full arc from brand conception through launch and beyond. |
215	| **Coordinates** | Contact information / project brief. |
